title: Clinical Co-Pilot — System Architecture
scope_summary: This document defines the end-to-end technical architecture for the Clinical Co-Pilot system across browser, OpenEMR, agent microservice, external LLM, and testing infrastructure. It specifies runtime boundaries, service interactions, API routes, state flow, and verification/observability layers used in production. It also records concrete implementation decisions such as auth validation, RBAC-driven tool separation, session scoping, and graceful degradation behavior. Overall, it acts as a technical system specification rather than a product requirements or tutorial document.
key_decisions_or_requirements: Deploy the AI agent as a separate FastAPI microservice in the same Docker network as OpenEMR.
Use FHIR R4 as primary clinical data access with REST fallback for unsupported resources.
Validate OpenEMR session tokens via /api/user instead of introducing a separate auth system.
Run a LangGraph retrieve-generate-verify loop with bounded retry for unverified responses.
Enforce role-based tool permissions, including distinct vitals and labs tool identities.
Bind AgentState to a single patient_id and reset on chart navigation to prevent context bleed.
Record incorrect-response feedback through POST /flag into Langfuse for auditability.
Degrade gracefully by showing an unavailable banner if the agent service is unreachable.
